id: 第四章-终点篇-大导寺信辅的前半生-六-朋友-p1

en: 第四章-终点篇-大导寺信辅的前半生-六-朋友
Shinsuke's rule for making friends was that the other person had to have talent.
u.src: 信辅交朋友的原则是对方必须有才能。

en: Even a morally upright gentleman, if he had no talent beyond his character, was to him a useless passerby.
u.src: 就算是品行端正的君子，如果除了品性之外没什么才能，对他来说都是没用的路人。

en: No, rather, whenever he saw such people, he naturally showed this attitude,
u.src: 不，毋宁说每次见到他们，他都自然的表现这种态度，

ja: からかわずにはいられなかった
en: and even could not help mocking these clowns.
u.src: 甚至不得不揶揄这些丑角。

en: With only six marks for conduct, as he went from middle school to high school, and from high school to university,
u.src: 操行分只有六分的他，从初中到高中，从高中到大学，

en: through the several stages of school life, he was always unable to keep from laughing at such people.
u.src: 在几个阶段的学校生活里，他总是不由的嘲笑那种人。

en: Among them, of course, there were some who became angry at this ridicule.
u.src: 他们之中当然有人对这种嘲笑感到愤怒。

en: However, there were also some who maintained the attitude of proper gentlemen toward this ridicule from beginning to end.
u.src: 不过，也有人对这种嘲笑始终保持正人君子的态度。

en: Being called an "unpleasant person" even made him feel, to some extent, pleased.
u.src: 对于自己被称为“令人讨厌的人”，他还多多少少感觉开心。

en: But when he mocked the other person however he could and still got no response at all,
u.src: 可是，不管怎么嘲讽对方，却得不到任何回应，

en: he could not help becoming angry.
u.src: 他就不得不愤怒了。

en: In fact, there once was one such gentleman--
u.src: 其实，曾经有过这样一个君子——

en: a humanities classmate from high school, an admirer of Livingstone.
u.src: 高中时候的一个文科同学，一个利文斯通的崇拜者。

en: When Shinsuke was living in the same school building as him,
u.src: 信辅在跟他住同一间校舍的时候，

en: he once said to him off the top of his head,
u.src: 曾经信口开河的对他说，

en: that even Byron, after reading Livingstone's biography, was moved until tears streamed down his face.
u.src: 连拜伦读了利文斯通的传记之后，也感动的流泪满面。

en: Twenty years had already passed since that time,
u.src: 从那个时候开始，到现在已经过去了二十年了，

en: and that admirer of Livingstone, in the journal of a certain Christian church,
u.src: 那个利文斯通的崇拜者在某基督教会机关志上，

en: was still singing the praises of Livingstone.
u.src: 还在歌颂斯文利通。
不仅仅是这样，

en: At the beginning of the article there was also a passage like this:
u.src: 文章的开头还有这样一段话：

en: "Even Byron, the demonic poet, read Livingstone's biography and was moved until tears streamed down his face;
u.src: “连恶魔诗人拜伦读了利文斯通的传记也感动的泪流满面，

en: what does this make us think of?"
u.src: 这让我们想到了什么呢？”

en: Shinsuke's rule for making friends was that the other person had to possess talent.
u.src: 信辅交朋友的原则是对方必须有才能。

en: Even if someone was a morally upright gentleman, if he had no intense pursuit of knowledge,
u.src: 就算是品行端正的君子，如果对知识没有强烈的追求，

en: to Shinsuke he was nothing more than a useless passerby.
u.src: 对他来说都是没用的路人。

en: He did not require his friends to be gentle or kind by nature.
u.src: 他不要求朋友性情温和善良。

en: Even if his friends lacked the passion of youth, he thought it did not matter.
u.src: 即使他的朋友没有青年人的热情，他也觉得无所谓。

en: No, rather, so-called good friends frightened him.
u.src: 不，不如说所谓的好朋友让他觉得害怕。

ja: っていなければならなかった
en: Therefore, all his friends had to have intellect.
u.src: 所以，他的朋友都一定得有头脑。
头脑——一颗清晰的的头脑。

en: He preferred clear-minded people to beautiful boys.
u.src: 他喜欢头脑清晰的人胜过美少年。

en: At the same time, he hated clear-minded people more than morally upright gentlemen.
u.src: 与此同时，他憎恶头脑清楚的人胜过品行端正的君子。

en: In fact, his friendships often mingled this hatred into the fervor of liking.
u.src: 事实上，他的友情常常都是在喜欢的热情里，掺杂这憎恶。

en: Even now, Shinsuke still felt that there was no friendship outside such passion.
u.src: 直到现在，信辅依然觉得在这种热情之外没有友情。

en: At the very least, he felt that outside such passion there was no friendship without the odor of Herr und Knecht, the German phrase literally meaning a master-servant relationship.
u.src: 他觉得至少在这种热情之外，没有不 Herr und Knecht（德语，直译为主仆关系）气味的友情。

en: Moreover, his friends at the time, seen from another side, were precisely enemies irreconcilable with him.
u.src: 况且他当时的朋友，从另一个方面说，正是与他势不两立的敌人。

en: He used his own intellect as a weapon and fought them constantly.
u.src: 他用自己的头脑当做武器，不断跟他们做斗争。

en: Whitman, free verse, creative evolution, the battlefield was everywhere.
u.src: 惠特曼、自由诗、创造的进化——战场无处不在。

en: On that battlefield, he defeated his friends or was defeated by them.
u.src: 在战场上，他打败他的朋友们，或者被他的朋友们打败。

en: This kind of spiritual battle undoubtedly became an act in which he gained joy through slaughter.
u.src: 这种精神上的战斗，毫无疑问成为了他通过杀戮获得喜悦的行为。

en: Yet it was also an undeniable fact that, in this process, new ideas and new images of beauty naturally revealed themselves.
u.src: 然而，在这个过程里自然展现的新观念和新的美感形象也是毫无疑问的事实。

en: How did the candlelight at three in the morning illuminate their debates?
u.src: 凌晨三点的烛光是怎样照耀他们的辩论的？

en: And how did the works of Mushanokoji Saneatsu dominate their arguments?
u.src: 武者小路实笃的作品又是怎样支配他们的论战的？

en: Shinsuke still remembered clearly that on one night in September, several very large moths flew toward the burning candle, and those dazzling moths suddenly appeared in the darkness.
u.src: 信辅还清楚的记得，在九月的某一个夜晚，有几只很大的飞蛾扑向了燃烧的蜡烛，绚丽夺目的飞蛾在黑夜中突然出现。

en: But once the moths plunged into the flame, they died in an inexplicable instant.
u.src: 但是，一旦飞蛾扑火，也就不可思议的瞬间死去了。

ja: ではなかったのだろう
en: Perhaps this was not anything very important either.
u.src: 可能这也不是什么大不了的事。

ja: められてしまうのだった
en: But even today, whenever Shinsuke recalls this small incident, whenever he recalls the life and death of those strangely beautiful moths, somehow the depths of his heart are seized by loneliness...
u.src: 但是，信辅一直到今天，只要一想起这件小事——只要一想起那不可思议的美丽飞蛾的生死，不知道怎么回事，他的内心深处就会被孤寂占领……

en: Shinsuke's principle in making friends was that the other person had to possess talent.
u.src: 信辅交朋友的原则是对方必须有才能。

ja: それだけにすぎなかった
en: That was the only standard he had.
u.src: 标准也就只有这个罢了。

ja: のないわけではなかった
en: However, even that standard was not without its exceptions.
u.src: 不过，那个标准也不是没有例外的时候。

en: Those exceptions were the class differences that cut off the friendship between him and his friends.
u.src: 那就是切断他和朋友之间友情的阶级差别。

en: Between Shinsuke and the middle-class youths who had grown up in the same sort of environment as he had, there was no barrier at all.
u.src: 信辅跟和他生长环境相同的中产阶级青年中间，没有任何隔阂。

en: But toward upper-class youths unfamiliar to him, and sometimes even toward youths of the upper middle class, he felt an unbelievable hatred, as if they were complete strangers.
u.src: 但是，跟和他不熟悉的上流阶级青年，有时候也会对中流上层阶级的青年，产生像陌生人一样的难以置信的憎恨干。

en: Among these people, some were lazy by nature, some were cowardly by nature, and some were lustful and self-indulgent.
u.src: 这些人当中，有些人生性懒惰，有些人生性怯懦，有些人好色纵欲。

ja: だけからではなかった
en: But it was not only for these reasons that he detested them.
u.src: 但是，他不仅仅是因为这些原因憎恶他们。

en: No, rather, he hated that incomprehensible indifference of theirs.
u.src: 不，毋宁说是憎恨他们那种不知所谓的漠然态度。

en: In truth, what he hated most was that indescribable incomprehensibility of theirs, something they themselves did not even notice.
u.src: 其实，他最憎恨的还是他们自己也没意识到的那种说不清的“不知所谓”。

en: Precisely because of this, he had an almost morbid concern for the lower classes, the people opposite to their class.
u.src: 正是因为这样，他对下层阶级——跟他们阶级相反的人群，有种几乎病态的关怀。

en: Shinsuke was full of sympathy for them.
u.src: 信辅对他们充满同情。

en: Of course, this sympathy was of no use at all.
u.src: 当然，这种同情毫无用处。

en: Every time he shook hands with those indescribably incomprehensible people, he felt as though needles were pricking his hand.
u.src: 每次跟那些说不清的“不知所谓”的人握手的时候，他都觉得如针刺手。

en: He remembered one afternoon in April, when a bitter wind was blowing, standing on the cliffs of Enoshima with his classmate, the eldest son of a baronial family, while Shinsuke was still in high school.
u.src: 记得在四月的某个午后，寒风凛冽，当时还在上高中的信辅和他的同学——一位男爵家的长子，一起伫立在江之岛的断崖之上。

en: Below their feet lay a coastline where the waves surged violently.
u.src: 脚下就是波涛汹涌的海岸线。

en: They threw a few copper coins into the sea and had several boys dive for them.
u.src: 他们往海里扔几个铜板，让几个少年“潜水”去捞。

en: Whenever the copper coins fell into the water, the boys jumped into the sea one after another with splashes of plop, plop.
u.src: 每当铜板落入海中，少年就相继“扑通，扑通……”的跳进海里。

en: Yet one ama stood below the cliff before a fire where dried seaweed was being burned, smiling as she gazed out over the surface of the sea.
u.src: 然而，有一个海女站在断崖下焚烧干海草的火堆前，笑着眺望海面。

en: This time, let's make that ama diver jump in with us too.
u.src: “这回让那个海女也一起跳进去吧。”

en: Shinsuke's friend wrapped a copper coin in the silver paper from a cigarette box, then suddenly turned around and flung it away with all his strength.
u.src: 信辅的朋友用香烟盒里的银色纸包着一枚铜币，然后猛一转身用力把铜币扔了出去。

en: The copper coin glittered as it fell into the surging sea.
u.src: 铜币闪闪发光，掉进了波涛汹涌的大海里。

en: At that very instant, the ama diver leapt into the sea ahead of the others.
u.src: 就在那一刹那，海女抢先跳进了海里。

en: Even now, Shinsuke still clearly remembered the cruel smile that had appeared at the corners of his friend's mouth.
u.src: 信辅直到现在，还清楚的记得他的朋友的嘴角浮现出的残忍笑容。

en: His friend possessed an extraordinary talent for foreign languages.
u.src: 他的朋友拥有过人的外语才能。

en: But he also certainly had extraordinarily sharp canine teeth...
u.src: 但是，他也确实有过人的尖利的犬齿……

en: Note: This story was originally planned to be three or four times as long as it is now.
u.src: 附记：这篇小说本来计划写成现在的三四倍长。

en: The content published this time naturally does not quite match the title The First Half of Daidoji Shinsuke's Life, but mainly because there was no other name to use instead, I had no choice but to keep this title.
u.src: 这次所发表的内容，和《大导寺信辅的前半生》的题目自然不相符合，主要因为没有其他名称可以替代，不得不沿用这个题目。

en: If this story can be regarded as one piece within The First Half of Daidoji Shinsuke's Life, that would be best of all.
u.src: 如果能够把这篇小说当做《大导寺信辅的前半生》里面的一篇，那就再好不过了。
